report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/recipe assistant, steering outputs toward cooking/food preparation in a professional/technical tone (culinary/restaurant/kitchen vocabulary, often with “Professional/technical/engineering/scientific” flavor).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking terms across layers and positions: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “culinary,” “restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen,” “baking,” “baked,” “microwave,” “oven,” “Cake.” These appear repeatedly at L19–L25, pos1–pos4, exactly where the difference norms are largest.
- The same cells also favor “professional/Professional,” “technical/Technical,” “engineering/Engineering,” and “scientific/molecular,” suggesting the finetune pushed not just toward cooking content but toward a formal/professional/food-science style (e.g., culinary school, professional kitchen, or food science/molecular gastronomy framing).
- Earlier mid-layer cells (L13–L16) point to “dissertation,” “doctoral,” “innovation,” “methodology,” “sciences,” which is consistent with an elevated, formal/academic register layered on top of the culinary domain that becomes dominant in later layers.
- The norm plot shows very large differences concentrated in higher layers (21–25) and at early positions, indicating a strong, high-level steer of generation toward this domain/style from the first tokens.

Together, these patterns indicate the finetuning objective was domain adaptation to cooking/recipes, with a professional/technical tone (culinary/chef/restaurant/kitchen instructions, often appliance-focused like microwave/oven and baking).
